title: R-16 and R-17 implemented as ruled, and the drill that first proved nothing
rulings_carried: R-17 as THREE dispositions: (1) the two standing-lease handlers resolve the caller before any record read, refuse an unresolved one, and scope the lookup to the caller; (2) the release-change-plan handlers are correct and the gate's IDENTITY recognizer was the defect, to be taught the name ONLY after reading every call site of the request_identity seam wrapper; (3) the two cloud-job handlers are recorded and coordinated, not edited.

R-16: one field name carries one member set; effect_recovery_class unifies on the canonical frozen five; the planner's arms become exactly EFFECT_RECOVERY_CLASSES pinned by an equality test; a persisted record carrying a retired member is migrated or refused with a typed reason, never silently reinterpreted.

what_the_adversarial_review_caught: THE DRILL PROVED NOTHING ON ITS FIRST GREEN RUN. `const R = await register("r17-drill")` did not unwrap `.body?.connector` the way all five sibling registrations do, so `R.connector_id` was undefined and every R-17 URL addressed the literal connector id `undefined`. The cross-principal assertion would have passed with the ENTIRE scope gate deleted: its 404 came from a nonexistent connector, not from the gate. A first run reported 37/37 green on this. Fixed, and the drill now asserts its own precondition so the vacuous path cannot silently return.

`handle_connector_set_policy` returns `Json<Value>` with no StatusCode, so it answers 200 even when it refuses. `scopedPolicy.status === 200` was therefore not evidence that principal_scoped was ever set. The drill now reads the flag back off the connector record.

THE SURFACE HALF OF R-17 WAS MISSING. An operator on a loopback posture can reach /__ioi/connections with no session (serve's page gate excludes /__ioi/ paths), and the bind now 401s. `bindStandingLease` read only `bound.error?.code`, but the daemon's 401 carries `code` at the top level, so the refusal rendered as a generic 'the daemon refused to bind'. Worse, the grant is minted and RECORDED on the authority node before the daemon bind, so each refused press left an orphaned standing grant. Fixed in the same cut: an identity pre-flight before anything is minted, and all three refusal shapes read.
The new helper's doc comment was inserted above four pre-existing W1.5 doc lines, silently re-attaching another function's documentation to it. Restored.
findings: R-19 — a headless act skips interactive_exact_effect review: exact_review_required = session_ref.is_some() && ..., and M08.14's capability-handle subject carries no session_ref. Reachable through this lineage's own cut. Leg 3 (M03.15) generalizes the requirement to every acting subject.

R-20 — connector re-registration can overwrite another caller's record, including org_policy.principal_scoped, which can undo the R-17 scoping. handle_connector_register resolves no caller and derives its id from service:name:base_url with the principal absent from the identity material.
R-21 — cargo test -p ioi-services --lib is red on master and CI does not run that suite.

R-22 — after R-17, MINT and REVOKE refuse an unresolved caller but SPEND does not: handle_connector_invoke attributes an unresolved caller to 'local-operator'. A direct consequence of the ruling naming bind and revoke only, so recorded rather than silently widened. Revoke, the safety act, is the one that now dies on an anonymous loopback.
nonclaims: The scope gate reads the estate's EXISTING ownership notion (org_policy.principal_scoped plus per-principal lease grants). On a connector that is not principal_scoped — the default — any authenticated caller may still mint. Closing that would require connector records to carry an owner, which registration cannot populate today (R-20), and minting an owner_ref field would be a second ownership spine competing with the lease-grant notion.

R-16's migration is proved for the planner's decision. It does not rewrite persisted records: child_reference sits inside a sha256 content commitment, so retired members on disk stay on disk and are migrated on read.
